title: Deduplicate overlapping patterns via node ID, keep first classification
context: Python method-less classes (dataclasses, Exception subclasses, Enums, TypedDicts, pydantic models) were invisible to the graph because the pattern required function_definition inside the class body. Adding a standalone class pattern to capture all classes risked duplicate symbols when both patterns matched the same node.
decision: Parse.ts keys pendingDefs by node id and retains only the first classification for each node. This allows a method-bearing class pattern (captures classes with methods) and a standalone class pattern (captures all classes) to coexist without duplication. Method-bearing matches take precedence, so child methods still classify as methods, not functions.
consequences: Method-less Python classes now appear in the graph with correct kind
Classes are never duplicated despite matching both patterns
Downstream analyses (blast radius, hunch why, not-calls conformance) now see complete graphs
Graph no longer silently weakens guards by omitting edges
alternatives_rejected: Merge duplicate symbols post-hoc in parse.ts (defers decision, higher complexity)
Single complex pattern for both forms (harder to maintain and extend)
Accept method-less classes as invisible (doesn't solve the problem)
